title: In Ephesians 4 What Does It Mean To Walk In A Manner Worthy Of Our Calling
paragraphs: Introduction: The Call to a Worthy Walk

Ephesians 4 marks a turning point in Paul’s letter. After laying a theological foundation about our identity in Christ (Ephesians 1–3), Paul shifts to practical instruction. He begins with an urgent appeal:
I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beseech you to walk worthily of the calling wherewith ye were called, - Ephesians 4:1 ASV
But what does it mean to "walk in a manner worthy of our calling"? Let’s explore Paul’s meaning, the practical implications, and how this shapes Christian living.
1. Understanding Our Calling

The "calling" Paul refers to is more than a generic invitation; it is God’s gracious call to salvation through Jesus Christ. This calling is rooted in God’s purpose and grace, not our own merit (Ephesians 1:18). It involves being chosen, redeemed, and adopted as God’s children. We are called to be saints—set apart for God’s glory.
who saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before times eternal, - 2 Timothy 1:9 ASV
2. What Does It Mean to "Walk Worthily"?

The word "walk" in Paul’s letters often refers to a person’s everyday conduct or lifestyle. To walk "worthily" (Greek: axios) means to live in such a way that our behavior aligns with the high position and purpose God has given us in Christ.
Importantly, this is not about earning God’s favor but responding to His grace. Our walk should reflect Christ’s transforming work in us.
3. The Marks of a Worthy Walk (Ephesians 4:2–3)
Paul immediately describes practical characteristics of a worthy walk:
Humility: Recognizing our dependence on God and valuing others above ourselves.
Gentleness: Responding to others with kindness and self-control.
Patience: Bearing with others, even when wronged or inconvenienced.
Forbearance in love: Willingness to put up with others’ shortcomings out of genuine love.
Unity of the Spirit: Eagerly seeking peace and maintaining the unity that the Holy Spirit creates among believers.
with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; giving diligence to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. - Ephesians 4:2–3 ASV
4. The Basis: Our Shared Identity in Christ
Paul grounds this worthy walk in the foundational truths of our unity in Christ:
One body
One Spirit
One hope
One Lord
One faith
One baptism
One God and Father of all

There is one body, and one Spirit, even as also ye were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all. - Ephesians 4:4–6 ASV
This unity is not something we create but something we are called to maintain, given by God Himself.
5. Practical Application: Living Out Our Calling
A worthy walk is demonstrated in relationships—with fellow believers, in our families, workplaces, and communities. It means:
Forgiving as we have been forgiven (Ephesians 4:32).
Speaking truth in love (Ephesians 4:15).
Using our gifts to build up the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:12).
Putting off the old self and living as new creations (Ephesians 4:22–24).
6. Empowered by Grace
Crucially, this worthy walk is only possible through the power of the Holy Spirit. God doesn’t call us to this walk and leave us to our own efforts. He provides the grace and strength needed:
for it is God who worketh in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure. - Philippians 2:13 ASV
Conclusion: Our High Calling and Daily Walk

To walk in a manner worthy of our calling is to live each day in light of who God has made us in Christ, empowered by His Spirit, and devoted to unity, love, and service. It’s a daily response to God’s grace—a life that reflects the gospel to the world.
